selected.rationale: The Fitness Enthusiast focuses on activewear, technical fabrics, and performance claims, perfectly matching the advertiser's technical backcountry ski shells and professional patroller-grade positioning.

The Sustainability Buyer expects supply chain transparency and high-quality materials, aligning with the advertiser's value of craftsmanship and the sustainable apparel affinities emphasized by the recommended publishers.
The Wellness Optimizer has low price sensitivity and demands science-backed claims, matching the premium $650+ price tier and the high-performance technical nature of the ski shells.

rejected.reason: The Busy Parent prioritizes subscriptions, household convenience, and family-friendly messaging, which conflicts with the advertiser's luxury one-off business model and technical outdoor gear category.
The Gen Z Aesthete has a typical AOV of $48 and seeks fast-moving trends and playful novelty, making them a poor fit for a $650+ luxury technical outerwear brand.
The Pet Parent focuses on pet food, pet supplies, and veterinary recommendations, which are completely irrelevant to human technical apparel and backcountry ski gear.
The Affluent Classic prefers classic apparel, home goods, and travel with understated heritage styling, rather than high-performance technical gear used by ski patrollers.
The Convenience-First Millennial is motivated by speed, instant delivery, and subscription services, which contradicts the advertiser's one-off purchase model for specialized ski equipment.
The Value-Conscious Shopper has a high price sensitivity and relies on discount-forward messaging and bundle offers, directly contradicting the advertiser's luxury $650+ price tier.

The Gifter is driven by gifting holidays, gift sets, and last-minute shipping wrappers, which is too transient and misaligned with the technical product-focused research required for backcountry gear.
